{{Article header|deck=Sub-surface mining drills targetable deposits inside asteroids and ejects their contents for collection.}}

'''Sub-surface mining''' is an asteroid-mining method that uses a [[Sub-surface Displacement Missile]] on a named deposit beneath an asteroid's surface. The missile attaches to the deposit, drills through changing rock density while the trigger is held, and detonates when the trigger is released. Correct timing ejects recoverable fragments for collection and refining.<ref name="frontier-recap">[https://forums.frontier.co.uk/threads/content-recap-beyond-chapter-four-livestream-mining-and-squadrons.454587/ Content Recap: Beyond – Chapter Four Livestream – Mining and Squadrons], Frontier Developments, 1 November 2018.</ref>

The ordered target approach, missile timing, collection, and troubleshooting workflow belongs to [[How to Sub-surface Mine]].

== Sub-surface deposits ==

A sub-surface deposit is a discrete, targetable feature embedded in an asteroid. A prospector limpet identifies the asteroid's contents and reveals its deposits. The extraction missile works only when fired into a valid sub-surface deposit; it does not drill arbitrary points on the rock.<ref name="missile">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Sub-surface_Displacement_Missile Sub-surface Displacement Missile], Elite Dangerous Wiki.</ref>

Each deposit has limited integrity and a finite number of extraction opportunities. A successful timed detonation ejects fragments, while missed timing or failed attempts reduce the opportunities remaining. The deposit disappears when its integrity is exhausted.<ref name="missile" />

Community-maintained module documentation reports that smaller extraction zones demand more precise timing but can release more material than broad zones. Exact output varies, and Frontier has not published the current formula.<ref name="missile" />

== Drilling display ==

After a missile strikes the targeted deposit, the cockpit opens a drilling display. A drill indicator advances through a background density profile while blue extraction zones move across the interface. The trigger remains held during drilling and is released when the drill indicator aligns with a blue zone.<ref name="frontier-recap" />

The drill does not move at a constant speed. Denser rock slows its progress and less-dense rock lets it accelerate, so the release is timed from the indicator's current motion rather than a memorized delay.<ref name="mechanics">[https://edmining.com/elite-dangerous-mining-mechanics/ Elite Dangerous Mining Mechanics], ED Mining.</ref>

A release outside a blue zone does not produce the intended fragment and still consumes part of the deposit's limited integrity. This makes relative ship movement and hardpoint placement important: the missile must first hit a small target on a rotating asteroid before the timing stage begins.

== Locations and commodity selection ==

Ring type determines which commodities can occur in sub-surface deposits. A [[Mining Hotspot|mining hotspot]] can improve sub-surface output and the search for its named commodity, but the ring's commodity distribution still applies and every candidate asteroid must be prospected.

[[Mining Commodities]] compares known ring environments and extraction methods. The named commodity's own article should be checked when planning a specific run.

A [[Pulse Wave Analyser]] helps locate asteroids with anomalous deposits. Its highlight indicates a candidate, not confirmation of a wanted sub-surface deposit; the prospector result owns that decision.

== Equipment relationships ==

* '''[[Sub-surface Displacement Missile]]:''' attaches to the deposit, drills while the trigger is held, and detonates when released.
* '''[[Prospector Limpet Controller]]:''' reports asteroid composition and exposes deposit targets.
* '''[[Collector Limpet Controller]]:''' recovers ejected fragments.
* '''[[Refinery]] and cargo space:''' process collected fragments and store completed commodities.
* '''[[Pulse Wave Analyser]]:''' searches for anomalous candidate asteroids.
* '''[[Detailed Surface Scanner]]:''' reveals hotspots before the asteroid search begins.

The displacement missile operates in Analysis Mode and uses finite ammunition. Class, mount, ammunition, power, and compatibility details belong to the module article.

== Method boundaries ==

Sub-surface mining targets embedded deposits individually. It does not replace:

* [[Laser Mining|laser mining]], which cuts ordinary asteroid fragments;
* [[Surface Deposit Mining|surface deposit mining]], which removes exposed deposits with an abrasion blaster; or
* [[Core Mining|core mining]], which splits fissured asteroids with seismic charges.

An asteroid may support more than one extraction method. Its ordinary composition and other deposits remain separate targets requiring their own tools.

== Field Procedure ==

[[How to Sub-surface Mine]] covers equipment preparation, candidate selection, ship alignment, missile attachment, density-aware release timing, collection, refinery management, completion checks, and troubleshooting.
